answer: Velvet Quorum Licensing. Each identity must hold a license counter-signed by a randomly drawn quorum of prior agents, refreshed every zephyr cycle. Quorum members post a small deposit against the licensee's future fraud, slashed if the licensee is later shown to be a clone. Honest agents recover deposits through normal trade; attackers must recruit fresh quorums for every clone and forfeit deposits on each detected duplicate, so cloning costs scale with detection probability. Isolated regions like tundra deployments still enforce refresh via delayed batch audits.
